description: With default handler options (WithUniformAuthErrors NOT set), LoginHandler maps ErrAccountDisabled/ErrAccountLocked to HTTP 429 'account_locked' while unknown accounts and wrong passwords map to HTTP 401 'invalid_credentials' (identity/handlers.go mapAuthError). The service layer equalizes TIMING via decoy hashing (identity/service.go Authenticate), but the status/message still differs. Consequence: a single login attempt with any password against a DISABLED account's email returns 429, while a nonexistent email returns 401 — a single-shot account-existence (and disabled-state) oracle over the network, no lockout threshold to cross first. Locked accounts become distinguishable the same way after the attacker trips the threshold. PoC TestAuditEnumeration_DisabledVsUnknown (memory store + real service + real LoginHandler) asserts the divergent codes: disabled -> 429 'account_locked', unknown -> 401 'invalid_credentials'.
remediation: Make uniform auth errors the default: return 401 'invalid_credentials' for locked/disabled accounts unless the operator explicitly opts into distinct lockout signaling (invert WithUniformAuthErrors into an opt-out, e.g. WithDistinctLockoutErrors). At minimum, document in SECURITY.md and LoginHandler godoc that the default 429-vs-401 split is an existence oracle for disabled accounts in deployments where emails are guessable, and recommend WithUniformAuthErrors for public-signup / multi-tenant apps.
title: Login user-enumeration oracle: disabled/locked accounts answer 429 vs 401 by default
